sources.role: official archived Hyper-V/OpenCore source and EFI template
official Windows/Hyper-V installation and VM settings guide
pinned OpenCore configuration template; the distribution guide places it in UEFI.VHDX
Hyper-V VM persistence and controller boundary

paths.path: Mounted UEFI.VHDX\EFI\OC\config.plist (the repository template is EFI - Testing/EFI/OC/Config.plist)
paths.naming: OpenCore plist; the installation guide says to mount UEFI.VHDX and edit config.plist with ProperTree. VM processor, memory, firmware boot order and integration-service settings are configured in Hyper-V's VM settings UI, not in a portable Lunchbox file.

paths.path: Hyper-V VM Integration Services and virtual keyboard/mouse devices configured in Hyper-V Manager; no project-owned mapping file.
paths.naming: The pinned guide enables all Integration Services. The project explicitly supports keyboard and trackpad/touchscreen/stylus input, with touchscreen/stylus passed as mouse input; USB and Bluetooth passthrough are explicitly unsupported. No gamepad mapping or stable physical-device identity is serialized.

paths.path: User-selected Hyper-V virtual hard disk (.vhdx) attached as the macOS guest disk; guest saves persist inside its APFS filesystem.
paths.naming: The Hyper-V wizard lets the user choose the virtual-disk name, size, and location; the installer formats that Msft Virtual Disk Media as APFS. There is no emulator save sidecar or host-visible per-title filename grammar. File transfer without USB uses a separate user-created VHDX mounted alternately by Windows and the VM.
evidence: source:balopez83/macOS_On_Hyper-V@cacf043c6b362c621037d44a85ad15feca9ef7aa README.md (this is a VM support project, not a guest save implementation)

paths.path: No emulator save-state file or slot path. Hyper-V Checkpoints are explicitly disabled by the installation guide.
paths.naming: No project-defined state filename grammar; Hyper-V checkpoints are VM-management state and are not enabled by this guide.

paths.path: Mounted UEFI.VHDX\EFI\BOOT and \EFI\OC (OpenCore UEFI bootloader and drivers); the template includes EFI binaries and config.plist.
paths.naming: UEFI.VHDX is the boot disk supplied by the project; no firmware checksum contract for a complete release VHDX is published in the pinned repository. The guide separately copies a version-specific com.apple.recovery.boot folder onto that mounted disk.

paths.path: No external cryptographic/decryption-key file is defined by the Hyper-V project.
paths.naming: Not applicable; OpenCore config and macOS recovery assets are boot/installation data, not a key-file contract.

linux.reason: The pinned project is a Windows Hyper-V host guide and does not publish a Linux host implementation or package.

linux-flatpak.reason: Hyper-V and its Windows VM-management UI are prerequisites; no Flatpak package or Linux virtualization contract is published.

macos.reason: The pinned project targets macOS as a guest under Windows Hyper-V; it does not publish a native macOS host package or virtualization backend.

notes: This is a Windows Hyper-V/OpenCore VM support project, not a conventional emulator. Its source-backed boundary covers the mounted UEFI.VHDX OpenCore configuration and boot assets, but it has no standalone gamepad mapper, host save/state format, or portable VM-settings writer. The repository was archived by its owner; its README recommends the more actively maintained OSX-Hyper-V project.
